svg.title: P006 · Most expensive products sold at full price
svg.desc: One row per full-price product, up to ten. Mug and Lamp have equal known prices. Mystery gives NULL and Bottle gives false. The filter keeps the two true comparisons. Products 3 and 4 leave the result. Lamp costs 150 and Mug costs 100. Only two products qualify for the ten available places. FROM Products · one table is enough. A product row contains both prices used to decide whether it is full price. That same row supplies its ID, name, brand and sale price for the ranking.
svg.text: Most expensive products sold at full price
One row per full-price product, up to ten.
Does a missing sale price prove the product was sold at full price?
A triangle marks an example to follow. A dark source band spans its columns. ƒ marks a calculated value. Deeper cell colors mark the values to
follow. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.
Can the two prices be compared?

g.aria-label: FROM Products · one table is enough
g.text: FROM Products · one table is enough
A product row contains both prices used to decide whether it is full price. That same row supplies its ID, name, brand
and sale price for the ranking.

svg.text: Mug and Lamp have equal known prices. Mystery gives NULL and Bottle gives false.
Which rows qualify as full price?
The filter keeps the two true comparisons. Products 3 and 4 leave the result.
Lamp costs 150 and Mug costs 100. Only two products qualify for the ten available places.
ORDER BY Sale_Price DESC, ProductID ASC LIMIT 10
